coding.note: The text extraction mixes the two page columns line by line, so many sentences are broken up. I chose quotes from single-column lines, table rows and captions so they can be matched word for word. Some of these quotes are thin, such as the denoising claim. Ablations: the future n-gram objective gets YES because Table 6 compares n=1, 2 and 3 with the same 6-layer architecture, Wikipedia+BookCorpus data and 125k steps. N-stream attention gets PARTIAL because it is never tested apart from the objective; the only evidence is the no-pre-training comparison against a vanilla Transformer, which changes both things at once. Denoising was adopted from MASS and has no ablation. Comparator scores in Tables 1-4 appear next to citations, and the paper never says whether they were copied or rerun, so I coded both rerun and scores_copied as NR. Compute: the paper names 16 V100 GPUs but gives no training duration, so compute_disclosed is N. Tokens: the token count could be derived from batch size, steps and sequence length, but the paper never states it, so tokens_disclosed is N. Data: the 160GB corpus is described only by category (news, books, stories, web text, with RealNews swapped in for CC-News) and no mixture proportions are given, so data_disclosure is PARTIAL.
